 Oral Judgment
1. Heard the learned counsels for the parties.

2. This appeal is preferred by the Insurance company assailing the Judgment and award dated 11.04.2022 passed in MVC No.205/2020 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Shorapur (for short 'the Tribunal') awarding compensation to the claimant.
3.
For the sake of convenience, the parties will be referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.
4. The relevant facts for adjudication of this appeal are that, the claimant is the owner of the 104 members of sheep and goats.

On 20.12.2019, the claimant while taking the sheep and goats for grazing and when all of them NC: 2026:KHC-K:949 HC-KAR reached near Tinthani Bridge on Lingasugur-Shorapur main road, a Ashok Leyland Tipper bearing registration No.KA- 36/B-7895 being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and the said vehicle ran over 104 sheep and goats and being aggrieved by the same, the claimant has filed MVC No.205/2020 before the Tribunal seeking compensation.
The said petition was contested by the respondents.
5. In order to prove the case, the claimant himself was examined as P.W.1 and produced 11 documents and same were marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11.
Two witnesses were examined on behalf of the respondents and four documents were produced as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R4.

The Tribunal after considering the material on record by its Judgment and award dated 11.04.2022, awarded compensation of Rs.14,96,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of Iffco-Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd vs Beerappa And Anr on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29374648/
2 petition till the date of realization.

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the same, the claimant has filed this appeal.

6. Heard Sri. Subhash Mallapur, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri. Krupa Sagar Patil,
learned counsel for the respondent No.1.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:949 HC-KAR 7.

It is argued by the learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance company that, the tribunal has failed to consider the fact that, the claimant himself has also contributed towards the occurrence of the accident and the said aspect has been ignored by the tribunal and accordingly sought for interference of this Court.
8. It is also stated that, the vehicle in question is falsely implicated in the alleged accident and accordingly sought for interference of this Court.
9. Per contra, Sri. Krupa Sagar Patil, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.1 sought to justify the impugned Judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

10. Having taken note of the submission made by the learned counsel for the parties, it is not in dispute as to death of 104 members of sheep and goats on 20.12.2019 on account of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.KA-36/B-7895.
11. On perusal of the police records, the same would indicate that, the vehicle in question is involved in the accident NC: 2026:KHC-K:949 HC-KAR and it has ran over 104 sheep and goats.
In that view of the matter, I am of the view that, the contentions raised by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant cannot be accepted.

12. Insofar as the award of compensation is concerned having taken note of the finding recorded by the Tribunal on Issue No.2, I am of the view that, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper which does not call for any interference by this Court.
13. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.
The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal, forthwith.

Sd/-
